title: consul 1.19.0 breaks all tags
body:
#### Overview of the Issue

after upgrading to version 1.19 I have lost the ability to use tags, because it started behaving in an odd way. 

For instance, my consul domain is: `<redacted-host>`

My consul server is: `<redacted-host>`

Whichever string I add to the left, it's being resolved successfully. 

For instance `<redacted-host>` works and it resolves to the same IPs of `<redacted-host>`

`<redacted-host>` works as well. 

I had tags to specify primaries and standby nodes, and all the tags where broken, because primary was associated to all the hosts in the pool. 

for instance, I was creating `<redacted-host>` and `<redacted-host>`, but both records where resolving either as standby and primary. 

this is what happened: 

```bash
dig <redacted-host> @participant7.0.0.1 -p8600 -t SRV +short

1 1 8300 <redacted-host>.
1 1 8300 <redacted-host>.
1 1 8300 <redacted-host>.
```

```bash
dig <redacted-host> @participant7.0.0.1 -p8600 -t SRV +short

1 1 8300 <redacted-host>.
1 1 8300 <redacted-host>.
1 1 8300 <redacted-host>.
```

I downgraded to 1.18.2, and it started working again.  

---

#### Reproduction Steps

upgrade from 1.18.2 to 1.19.0

comments.author: participant1
comments.body: This should be resolved with the linked PR. We're discussing putting out 1.19.1 sooner than expected. BOLO for that release.

comments.author: participant2
comments.body: Hey guys, hope you don't mind me jumping in here. How is it there hasn't been an emergency release pushed out already? This isn't some trivial thing that broke, it is the most fundamental function of Consul to have working correctly.

comments.author: participant3
comments.body: At the chance of this being basically a +1, I entirely agree with @participant2. This is the most fundamental functionality of Consul and the longer Hashicorp waits to cut a release, the more clusters will just stop working on some very unexpected fashion. Hashicorp _needs_ to rush out a patched release.

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
I would like to ask to delete the existing release which breaks the consul cluster for everyone. 
Until this version is available for download, someone will try to install it. 
And this is not a minor issue: in my case all the Postgres servers became masters and standby at same time.

comments.author: participant4
comments.body: Wow, I just ran into the same issue. Luckily, it was only in the dev environment. It's surprising that this bug has been around for so long without a fix. I'm really hoping it gets addressed soon!

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
@participant1 hi 😸 What do you think? 
If I were you, I would delete these releases, because they should not be downloaded and installed by anyone. While I am writing, maybe someone else is installing it and he's facing an outage.

comments.author: participant5
comments.body: Same as @participant4, I caught it in my dev cluster, but it took me way to long to find this thread and I was almost convinced that I was insane. This is the last time that I go to cutting edge simply because I was notified that a newer version existed.

comments.author: participant4
comments.body: It seems that this is still an issue in version 1.19.1 :-(

comments.author: participant1
comments.body: @participant4 let me see if I can reproduce. If you have any interesting details, let me know. One special case that might be interesting: do you have any periods in the tag name? e.g. `this.is.my.tag.foo.service.consul`

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
@participant4 I tried manual testing with 1.19.1 and couldn't reproduce the issue. I also believe the new tests I added should be exercising a similar case. Maybe we could dig into your environment more. I see from the UI this server is running 1.19.1. Is it possible you're running the DNS query against a client agent or another server? In that case, would all agent you are hitting also be updated to 1.19.1?

This is actually my last day at Hashi, but I've alerted others to 👀 this thread.

comments.author: participant6
comments.body: @participant4 on top of what Dan asked I am curious if you can recognize differences in the service registration or another aspect of the test [TestDNS_ServiceAddressWithTagLookup](https://github.com/hashicorp/consul/blob/9f62fb4113d286a5642dff9da0138aa3bbef05da/agent/dns_service_lookup_test.go#L388).  I have tried variations of this test such as adding your DNS config with allowing stale, resitering services that have nodes, using a prepared query, and I am not able to replicate this locally.  I would love any information you have about how the service registration or something else is different.

comments.author: participant4
comments.body: Hi guys! My bad, the servers hosting the service were running version 1.19.1, but my DNS resolvers were not. After updating the resolvers, everything is working fine now. Sorry for the confusion, and thanks for your reactivity :) Good luck for what comes next @participant1

comments.author: participant6
comments.body: that's great to hear @participant4.  thank you for the feedback.  closing issue.
